## Part A - Arithmetic Operations

```{r}
b <- 5

a - b
a * b
a / b

```

#Part 2

```{r}
a %% b
a %/% b
```

#Part 4 

#Question 1

#The division gives you the exact result, while the other two operators break down into the remainders.

```{r}

17 %% 5
17 %/% 5
```

## Part Basic Data Types: typeof(), class(), and mode()

#Part 2
```{r}
x <- 42
typeof(x)
y <- 42L
typeof(y)
z <- "42"
typeof(z)
w <- TRUE
typeof(w)
v <- 3 + 2i 
typeof(v)
```

#Part 3
```{r}
x <- 42
class(x)
y <- 42L
class(y)
z <- "42"
class(z)
w <- TRUE
class(w)
v <- 3 + 2i 
class(v)
```

#Part 4
```{r}
x <- 42
mode(x)
y <- 42L
mode(y)
z <- "42"
mode(z)
w <- TRUE
mode(w)
v <- 3 + 2i 
mode(v)
```

#Part 5

#Question 3: x is stored as a decimal number by default, while y uses the L suffix to force R to store it strictly as a whole number.

#Question 4:Yes, they differ for x because typeof(x) describes its precise format, whereas class(x) and mode(x) describe its mathematical term ("numeric").


## Part C — Type Conversion (20 min)

```{r}
num_string <- "123"
num_value <- as.numeric(num_string)
typeof(num_value)
class(num_value)
mode(num_value)
```

#Part 2
```{r}
logical_zero <- as.logical(0)
logical_one  <- as.logical(1)
logical_zero
logical_one
```

#Part 3
```{r}
bad_string <- "hello123"
result <- as.numeric(bad_string)
```
